follow_ups: Add two-call clobber probe to the guard for every pointer-returning builtin and lib function.
Remove the stale char_buf BSS comment in the compiler (misclassifies anka_akshar as static).
suchi_vardh/avali_pravesh old-buffer leak noted (leak, not dangle; owner decision about who frees).

ws1.verdict: Library clean: every pointer a lib function returns is heap (nirmmita), lives for the program

ws2.anka_akshar: stack scratch below rsp (d*): sub rsp,16; mov [rsp],al; mov byte [rsp+1],0; mov rax,rsp; add rsp,8 -> returned pointer is rsp-8 in just-freed space; char_buf BSS comment stale (no such symbol); next push/call writes exactly at rsp-8

v298_fix.anka_akshar: stable buffer: (66)->B, (97)->a, survives a later sandhi call (still B)
v298_fix.vartani_sandhi: literal now refuses at compile time (E_VARTANI_STHIRA, hint: s+t new string or nirmmita+pratilip+sandhi); mutable buffer still mutates in place (b=abcd, s=abcd, same buffer, by design)

ws2.vartani_sandhi: caller-provided, mutated in place: scans dst to NUL, copies src incl terminator, returns dst; no allocation; defect is mutation+aliasing; crashes iff dst is read-only literal (PE 0xC0000005), silent corruption on Linux; NOT a lifetime defect; brief premise corrected (does NOT return its own stack frame)
ws2.windows_p_vs_b: dangling stack-scratch byte overwritten by whatever the next call pushed on PE (observed P=80 vs Linux B=66); mechanism proven, exact overwriting value platform/call-sequence-dependent

ws3_cheapest_linux_test: Two-call clobber probe: call, then call another function (pushes/calls, overwriting the freed stack slot), then read the first result; if it changed, it is a dangling stack pointer (as R120 ws2_anka2 did). GUARD_PAGES would not catch it (freed frame still mapped, read does not fault); heap poisoning would not (not heap); stack canary would not (catches smashing, not dangling reads).
